title: Put a one-line entry rule on every table row
problem: A reader cannot tell at a glance whether an event is a freezeout, a re-entry or simply unknown.
options: Keep the three-way label (confirmed / multi-entry / unverified)
Add a plain-English sentence per row ('You may buy in again until 4:55 PM')
Add a colour-coded badge and drop the text
effect: The second option costs one more column and removes most misreads. It does not change any data.

title: Ask the poker rooms for a written single-entry statement
problem: Silence on a structure sheet is not a one-entry promise, so nothing can be confirmed as a freezeout.
options: Email each room's tournament desk and publish the reply with a date
Photograph the printed structure sheet in the room on the day
Leave the rows unverified and plan around them
effect: Only the first two can move an event from unverified to confirmed. Until then a freezeout plan is an assumption.

title: Capture dated hotel quotes instead of a single number
problem: Room rates move daily; a single figure goes stale and the true nightly cost with it.
options: Keep the dated rate log and paste a new quote each time you check
Add a screenshot field per log entry
Show only the resort fee and tax, which are stable
effect: The log is the only option that keeps a like-for-like history. Screenshots make disputes resolvable.

title: Time the walks yourself and record them
problem: No official source publishes hotel-to-poker-room walking times, so the 30-minute filter is nearly empty.
options: Record the walking time you measure and store it with a date
Only accept on-property hotels until a walk is measured
Accept a third-party routing estimate and label it as an estimate
effect: The first option makes the filter useful and stays honest. The third fills the table but is not an official value.

title: Run the official-source check every morning, not once a day at random
problem: Schedules, structures and fees change without notice.
options: GitHub Actions cron at 13:00 UTC (6 AM Las Vegas) every day
Twice daily (06:00 and 18:00 Las Vegas)
Weekly
effect: A morning run matches the brief's 'pull the schedule each morning'. Twice daily catches intraday changes at double the Actions minutes.

title: Publish one site instead of thirteen session dashboards
problem: Earlier sessions each left a dashboard in its own folder; the same question has several different answers.
options: Keep this root site as the single answer and demote the rest to an archive index
Keep every dashboard and add a comparison page
Delete the older dashboards
effect: The first option gives one answer per question and keeps earlier work reachable. Deleting loses source history.

title: Price a plan that assumes one entry, and one that assumes re-entry
problem: A multi-entry event can cost two, three or more buy-ins; a plan that assumes one entry understates the cost badly.
options: Show both totals side by side on the planner
Show only the single-entry total
Show a range with no assumptions stated
effect: Side-by-side totals make the downside visible before you commit money.

title: Reconfirm everything before any non-refundable payment
problem: Every value here is a snapshot from an official page on 2026-11-17.
options: Re-run the source check and read the change log before booking
Call the room and the hotel to confirm
Book a refundable rate only
effect: Refundable rates are the cheapest insurance; Caesars and Horseshoe advertise free 48-hour cancellation and Resorts World requires 48 hours' notice for a deposit refund.

title: Capture dated stay quotes automatically in the morning job
problem: The dated rate log currently holds hand-captured booking-engine snapshots; the trip planner stays Incomplete without a quote for the chosen dates and occupancy.
options: Extend the morning job to open each official booking link with fixed dates/occupancy and store whatever total the page shows (may fail: booking engines are JavaScript apps)
Keep captures manual but require a screenshot/link + timestamp before any booking decision
Subscribe to official rate-alert emails and log them as dated entries
effect: A fresh dated quote per hotel per morning would make true nightly cost comparable like-for-like and let the planner complete honestly.

title: Adopt a like-for-like comparison policy before any hotel ranking
problem: Existing captures differ in stay window and occupancy (2 adults Dec 2-9 vs 1 adult Dec 13-20), so 'cheapest hotel' cannot be derived from them.
options: Rank nothing until two hotels share dates, occupancy and room class
Rank with an explicit comparability grade per row
Rank on nightly average and mark differing occupancy
effect: Prevents a false ranking; the flagged page already refuses to name a cheapest hotel.

title: Decide how walking minutes get verified
problem: No official source publishes walking times between properties; the brief wants a 30-minute walking filter.
options: Keep minutes blank + provide one-click walking-direction links (current)
Record user-measured minutes via the routes page recorder (already available, browser-only)
Add a maps-distance service to the morning job and label its output as third-party estimates
effect: The 30-minute filter can only be honest about measured or officially stated minutes.

title: Decide the fate of the 13 archived session dashboards
problem: Earlier session folders are published alongside the root site and disagree with it on some numbers.
options: Keep linked as read-only archives (current)
Move archives out of the published tree into git history only
Add a banner to each archive page pointing at the root site as the source of truth
effect: Reduces reader confusion when an archived page shows an older verdict count.

title: Publish one root-site generator (done here) and retire the second one
problem: Two scheduled jobs each rebuilt the root site from different data with different verdict standards, so the published headline changed every night depending on which job committed last.
options: One canonical builder + an integration step, and a CI guard that fails when the committed site is not the canonical output (chosen, implemented)
Give each session its own subdirectory and never let a scheduled job write the root
Freeze the scheduled rebuilds entirely and rebuild only by hand
effect: The site is reproducible: `python3 scripts/integrate_b3be876c.py && python3 scripts/build_ea99006a.py` regenerates every published page, and quality.yml proves the committed output matches.

title: Keep value-level monitoring, drop hash-level alarmism
problem: Hashing a whole casino page produces a 'change' on every request (tokens, timestamps), which buries real edits in noise; 48 of 96 ledger entries were 'changed' on the first run.
options: Compare extracted official sentences per value (implemented)
Keep page hashes but label them informational (kept)
Diff rendered text with a normalisation pass before hashing (future)
effect: A row is marked 'source changed' only when the sentence behind its value changes.

title: Settle the 8 a.m. requirement before the hotel is booked
problem: The brief's day is meant to start at 8 a.m.; no captured Strip schedule publishes an enterable start before 09:10, and the recommended window's first two days start at 11:00 (F57). That changes what a hotel is for: a 9:10 start needs a different lobby than an 8:00 start.
options: Accept the published starts and plan from them (what the site does now)
Ask the Venetian room by phone whether an unlisted early turbo exists, and record the answer with the date and the name that gave it
Move the window to a series whose schedule carries earlier flights and let the site re-rank
effect: One of the three has to be picked before the non-refundable hotel payment: the site will not invent an 8 a.m. event to make the plan look complete.

title: Decide where parking and the incidental hold belong in 'true cost per night'
problem: The Venetian now publishes $20/night guest self-parking and a $150/night incidental hold. Parking is a real cost of driving, but it is waived for the day with 3+ hours of play, and the incidental hold is not a cost at all - it is a card hold that is released.
options: Keep them as separate lines next to the nightly rate, as now (chosen: nothing is folded into an average that would make two hotels look comparable when they are not)
Fold parking into the true nightly cost and mark the row 'assuming you drive'
Drop parking from the site and let the reader add it
effect: The planner already adds parking when the box is ticked and states the source; the choice is whether the headline 'true cost per night' should include it. Whichever is picked, the incidental hold stays out of the cost and in the terms column.

title: Keep the DOM smoke test as a publish gate, not an ad-hoc check
problem: scripts/dom_smoke_0fd4c550.mjs found three real defects in hours because it runs the published JavaScript against the published pages, and it is now a step in recheck-ea99006a that runs before the commit. It is optional in `npm test` because jsdom has to be installed for it, so today a contributor running only the unit tests does not see it.
options: Leave it as a pre-publish gate that skips when jsdom is missing (current state)
Add jsdom to devDependencies so `npm test` always runs it
Port the assertions to the existing unit tests and delete the DOM harness
effect: Option 2 costs an npm install in CI and catches interaction bugs on pull requests instead of at publish time; option 3 loses the property that makes it useful, which is testing the JavaScript that actually ships.

title: Re-read the recommended window live, on a schedule, instead of by hand
problem: scripts/verify_window_0fd4c550.py compares the published rows with a transcription that this session read off the official page on 2026-11-19. CI re-runs that comparison every morning, which proves internal consistency - but it cannot notice the room changing the schedule, because the left-hand side is a file rather than a fetch.
options: Keep the dated manual read, which is what the site claims today
Teach the morning scraper to parse the schedule page itself and diff against the published rows, so a start-time change becomes a flagged row without a human
Point the comparison at the daily capture that already exists in data/251c122f
effect: Option 2 or 3 would make the 6-13 December recommendation self-monitoring. Option 1 is honest but ages: the read is stamped 2026-11-19 and the site says so.
